bibl.title: Open-air Festivals and Cultural Cohabitation in Late Hellenistic Alexandria.
bibl.seg: Marie-Françoise Baslez, Open-air Festivals and Cultural Cohabitation in Late Hellenistic Alexandria.

Luca Arcari (ed.), Beyond Conflicts. Cultural and Religious Cohabitations in Alexandria and Egypt between the 1st and the 6th Century CE = Studien und Texte zu Antike und Christentum. 103 (Tübingen, 2017) pp. 307-322.
bibl.note: How Jews and Greeks coexisted in Late Hellenistic and Roman Alexandria. - 1. The political stake of royal festivities. - 2. The rejoicing festival: a mean of social interplay between Jews and Greeks. - 3. Open-air festivals: a widespread custom. - 4. Criteria and requirements for truly open festivals.
